summary: A 1931 ground-mounted L-4 cab on the Entiat Ridge, reached by a road built that year; removed or destroyed in 1967, with no source describing the summit today.

facts.design: Ground-mounted gable-roofed L-4 cab, the only structure on the site
facts.status_note: Cab removed or destroyed in 1967; no source describes what remains on the summit.

access.note: Drive-up on Forest Service roads per Washington Lookouts, which advises high clearance and notes that road conditions change. No gate is mentioned; current status not verified.

visit.trail_note: Eagle Creek Road to Van Creek Road (NF7520), then the Chumstick route for about eight miles to a short spur to the top.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Wenatchee National Forest

events.note: Site first developed as a heliograph lookout, also known then as Swakane.
Firelookout.com lists Roy Thurman as lookout in 1923; the list continues through 1965.
Ground-mounted gable-roofed L-4 cab built; the only structure on the site.
Wenatchee National Forest road crew built about six miles of road to the summit; a June 26, 1931 newspaper item calls it recently completed.
Road crew held a picnic on the summit; sources give June 14 (Washington Lookouts list) and July 14 (Willhite).
Swen Hansen served as lookout and reported record visitor counts in a 1933 Leavenworth Echo item.
Firetower.org says the cab was removed in 1967; Firelookout.com and Willhite say destroyed.
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register as US 1393 on August 22, 2012.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firetower.org says the cab was removed in 1967; Firelookout.com and Washington Lookouts say it was destroyed in 1967. The year agrees; the verb does not.
The 1931 picnic on the summit is dated June 14 in the Washington Lookouts list (quoting a newspaper) and July 14 on the Willhite page. Both are stated in the story.

sources.title: Chumstick Mountain Lookout Site, Former Fire Lookout Sites register

notes_for_editor: Removed vs destroyed in 1967 is unresolved and stated in the story. Summit condition today is not described by any source read; the directional-marker caption is the only current-site detail. Newspaper items spell the 1933-34 lookout Swen Hansen and Sven Hanson; the story avoids choosing one. The Mrs. Thurman / Roy Thurman link is not stated in any source. Page-read budget used: 6 fetch_text reads in total (Weebly page three times, Firetower.org, Firelookout.com and Willhite once each). The Weebly page's removal section and any National Geodetic Survey note were not legible in the reads, so the 1967 removal date rests on Firetower.org, Firelookout.com and Willhite. The WebSearch budget for this turn was exhausted, so no searches were run. Record elevation and coordinates match the register and were not otherwise checked.
